title: Slots queue: a hand-back tie-breaks on its own id and loses its place when two asks share an mtime
body:
CI run 45328303838 (3.5.2 candidate at 029297dee) failed intentsvcs estate::slots::tests::a_hand_back_keeps_its_place_from_a_grant_revoked_before_its_start at slots.rs:2835 on ubuntu-latest: the queue read [later, again] where [again, later] was expected.

`queue_order` sorts open requests by `asked_at`, or for a hand-back (`--place-of`) the prior request's `asked_at`, then by the request's OWN id. `asked_at` is the ask file's mtime, which Linux stamps from the coarse clock, so `first` and `later`, asked a few milliseconds apart, carried one mtime. The tie then fell to the ids, and the hand-back's own id, minted after `later`'s, sorted it behind the request whose place it was ahead of. This is a product ordering defect on Linux, not only a test flake: a hand-back can lose its place to a request asked in the same clock tick as the one it replaces.

Fix: the sort key is `(place.asked_at, place.id)`, the prior request's id as well as its time, with the request's own id as the last tie-break. The test pins the two asks to one mtime, so the tie is exercised on every platform.
